title: Invertibility of the explicit directed matching charts
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal U$ be a universe-small locally directed open cover of $X$ whose index category is thin. Give modules $M_i$ and normalized tensor-pullback transition isomorphisms $t_f$ satisfying the composition cocycle [def-pc-module-pullback]: for $f:i\to j$ and $g:j\to k$, $t_{g\circ f}$ is the composite of the equality transport along the specified equality between the transition maps, the normalized pullback composition comparison, the pullback of $t_g$, and $t_f$. For the explicit multiequalizer matching module $L$ and its canonical adjoint maps $c_i:(\mathcal U_i\to X)^*L\to M_i$ [def-trf-directed-tensor-matching-module], every $c_i$ is an isomorphism. This asserts a property of the constructed module and does not choose a descent object from an existence assertion. Taking the associated isomorphisms of these invertible maps gives the canonical chart isomorphisms, which satisfy the original normalized chart equation.

proof.text: For an open immersion the unit of the section-normalized tensor adjunction is bijective on every open contained in its image: compare with the standard pullback adjunction by uniqueness of left adjoints and use the standard unit formula. The comparison is itself invertible.

For P_i, the sheaf of sets underlying the pushforward of M_i, restriction to V intersection image(U_i) is bijective since its preimage in U_i is the same open as the preimage of V. The transition r_f is bijective on V contained in image(U_i): its factors are the unit on an open contained in image(trans f), the supplied t_f, and equality/composition transports. The tensor cocycle gives r_(f≫g)=r_g≫r_f by the mate-composition formula. Local directedness supplies exactly the common-lower image covering.

Evaluation at an open preserves the multiequalizer. Mathlib Multifork.IsLimit.sectionsEquiv therefore identifies its sections with the matching families. Apply the proved matching-sections theorem to see that projection to i is bijective on every V contained in the image of U_i.

For an open O of U_i take V=image(O) in X. The normalized unit from the matching module sections on V is bijective. Composing it with the canonical chart map is exactly the matching projection, also bijective by the previous step. Hence the chart is bijective on O, using preimage(image(O))=O. Sectionwise bijectivity proves it is an isomorphism, including empty opens. Define the canonical chart isomorphisms using the chart hom map and its inverse. Keep this definition irreducible and expose its hom map by a proved formula. Apply the comparison for four abstract isomorphism factors and their specified hom maps. The composite hom equation follows by the normalized mate calculation and the multiequalizer projection relation. Replay that short calculation here to avoid expensive kernel reduction when specializing its nested statement. This gives the exact normalized equation for these isomorphisms.

theorem tensorMatchingChart_isIso [Quiver.IsThin 𝒰.I₀]
    (ht : ∀ {i j k : 𝒰.I₀} (f : i ⟶ j) (g : j ⟶ k),
      t (f ≫ g) =
        eqToIso (congrArg (fun a ↦ (tensorPullback a).obj (M k)) (𝒰.trans_comp f g)) ≪≫
          (tensorPullbackSectionComp (𝒰.trans f) (𝒰.trans g)).app (M k) ≪≫
          (tensorPullback (𝒰.trans f)).mapIso (t g) ≪≫ t f)
    (i : 𝒰.I₀) : IsIso (tensorMatchingChart 𝒰 M t i)
